abstract: Conformal prediction can lose coverage when data are nonexchangeable, while nonsymmetric fitting invalidates its usual argument even with exchangeable observations. We extend full conformal prediction using prespecified calibration weights in [0,1], fixed algorithm tags, and a weighted random swap independent of the data. Calibration weights emphasize observations expected to resemble the test point; tags permit order-sensitive fitting without serving the same inferential role. The swap yields a finite-sample coverage lower bound of 1 - alpha minus a weighted sum of total-variation distances between original and swapped residual-vector distributions. Exchangeability eliminates this penalty even for nonsymmetric fitting; under nonexchangeability, small penalties limit undercoverage rather than guarantee nominal validity. With distinct residuals and small normalized test weight, the corresponding upper bound also limits overcoverage. Related bounds cover split conformal and jackknife+. Simulations and electricity data show that residual weighting improves coverage, while weighted least-squares fitting can narrow intervals. On ordered electricity data, coverage rises from 85.2% to 89.3% against a 90% target, whereas permuted controls show no width advantage. Election-data improvements remain below target, illustrating that a useful drift guarantee depends on residual-distribution similarity rather than weighting alone.
methods: Fix calibration weights w_i in [0,1] and algorithm tags before observing the data, normalize weights by D = 1 + sum_i w_i, and assign the test point weight 1/D. Draw K independently with these probabilities and swap the candidate test observation with position K while retaining tags at their positions. At the true response, miscoverage implies that K is a high-residual index in the residual vector fitted to the swapped sequence: replacing the test residual by infinity and using w_K <= 1 yields the required quantile comparison. For every residual vector, indices above its weighted (1 - alpha)-quantile carry total normalized weight at most alpha. Independence permits averaging the swapped-vector events over K. Each event probability differs from its original-vector counterpart by at most their total-variation distance. Summing gives miscoverage at most alpha plus the weighted swapped-residual discrepancy, without assuming algorithm symmetry or stability.
results: Table 2 distinguishes calibration from fitting on the electricity-transfer prediction task. In the original time order, unweighted full conformal with least squares attains 85.2% coverage against the 90% target, with mean width 0.565. Weighting calibration residuals while retaining least squares raises coverage to 89.0% but widens intervals to 0.606. Adding weighted least-squares fitting yields 89.3% coverage and width 0.527. Both weighted approaches remain below target; their contrast suggests that residual weighting improves calibration, whereas weighted fitting can improve interval efficiency. In the randomly permuted, exchangeable control, coverage is 89.9%, 90.8%, and 90.8%, respectively, with widths 0.639, 0.652, and 0.663. Thus, the width advantage does not persist when ordering is randomized. These averages over time support gains under the observed temporal structure, not a universal 90% guarantee under arbitrary drift. The theoretical justification for limited undercoverage depends on a small weighted swapped-residual total-variation term.
notes: Coverage is marginal over the data and random swap. Table 2 contains time-averaged coverage and widths, without uncertainty estimates or explicit width units; no significance or unit conversion is inferred. Weights and tags have distinct roles and are fixed for the stated theorem. Experimental descriptions cite equation (14) even for nonsymmetric fitting; the theorem applies to the randomized construction in equation (20). Small discrepancy controls undercoverage; limiting overcoverage additionally requires distinct residuals and a small normalized test weight. The jackknife+ guarantee starts at 1 - 2 alpha, not 1 - alpha.
